learningObjective: Explain why an ML compiler that ships a .so/.dll artifact must define a stable C ABI at the artifact boundary, not a C++ one, and what breaks when the boundary is not stable.
stem: An AOT-compiled artifact (e.g., AOTInductor .so, TensorRT plan loader, IREE HAL module) exposes an entry point that must be loaded by processes built with unknown compiler toolchains. Which ABI-boundary discipline is standard, and why?

options.text: ABI stability is unnecessary because dynamic loaders (dlopen/LoadLibrary) automatically rewrite mangled symbols to match the host process's C++ compiler, meaning any C++ boundary works.

The artifact exposes a mangled C++ ABI with `std::vector<Tensor>` return types because C++ standard library types are guaranteed to be layout-compatible across all major compilers (GCC, Clang, MSVC) since C++17.

The artifact exposes a C ABI (plain `extern "C"` functions with POD structs and opaque handles). C++ name mangling, exception ABIs, and STL types differ across compilers/versions and would break linking or crash at library boundaries.
The artifact must be statically linked into the host process and cannot use a dynamic library at all; ABI concerns only arise when linking, not when loading precompiled kernels.

explanation: C++ ABIs differ across compilers (GCC vs. MSVC), across libc++ vs libstdc++, and even across std versions. Name mangling, exception unwinding, and STL container layout are not portable. Serious dynamic-artifact stacks expose only a C ABI at the boundary: extern "C" entry points, POD structs, opaque handles created and destroyed on the artifact's side. Users can wrap that C ABI in a C++ facade inside the loading process, but the boundary itself is C.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: dynamic loaders do not rewrite mangled symbols; a mangled-symbol mismatch causes load-time or runtime linkage failure.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: `std::vector<T>` is not ABI-stable across compilers or STL implementations; passing it across .so boundaries is a known source of undefined behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: matches the standard practice used by AOTInductor's C shim, TensorRT's C++ header + C API split, CUDA driver API, and IREE HAL C.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: dynamic libraries are widely used; ABI concerns are exactly why they exist and why they use C boundaries.

assumptions: The artifact will be loaded by a process compiled with a different toolchain or C++ standard than the compiler used to build the artifact.
nonImplications: Does not imply that internal implementations must be C; only the boundary must be C.
Does not imply ABI stability is only about C++; issues also arise with GPU driver ABIs, but those are shipped by vendors.

distractorRationales.B: False stability claim about STL types.
